record.original_question: Let γ=(sqrt(5)-1)/2. For λ1, λ2 in C, define one-dimensional potentials s_j^{λ_j}(k)=λ_j χ_[1-γ,1)({kγ}) for j in {1,2}, and define V(m,n)=s_1^{λ_1}(m)+s_2^{λ_2}(n). Let H be the Schrödinger operator on l^2(Z^2) given by [Hψ](m,n)=ψ(m+1,n)+ψ(m-1,n)+ψ(m,n+1)+ψ(m,n-1)+V(m,n)ψ(m,n). Do there exist values of λ1 and λ2 for which the spectrum σ(H) is a Cantorval, meaning the spectrum is the closure of its interior and has no isolated connected component?

evidence.quote: Another example of a two dimensional problem arises when considering a two dimensional potential V that can be written as a sum of two one dimensional potentials s_{λ1}^1 and s_{λ2}^2. Here, λ1 , λ2 ∈ C and, for j ∈ {1, 2} and k ∈ Z, s_j^{λ_j} (k) := λj · χ[1−γ,1) ({kγ}) with γ = (sqrt(5)-1)/2. Thus, for any m, n ∈ Z, V (m, n) := s_1^{λ_1} (m) + s_2^{λ_2} (n). The corresponding Schrödinger operator H in the space l2 (Z2 ) is defined as follows : for ψ ∈ l2 (Z) and (m, n) ∈ Z2 , [Hψ](m, n) := ψ(m + 1, n) + ψ(m − 1, n) + ψ(m, n + 1) + ψ(m, n − 1) + V (m, n) · ψ(m, n).
Conjecture 2.1.2. There exist values of λ1 and λ2 such that the spectrum σ(H) of H is a Cantorval; that is, the spectrum is the closure of its interior and no connected component is isolated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let γ = (√5 − 1)/2, and for a real number x let {x} ∈ [0,1) denote its fractional part. For each j ∈ {1,2} and complex parameter λ_j ∈ ℂ, define the one-dimensional potential s_j^{λ_j} : ℤ → ℂ by
  s_j^{λ_j}(k) := λ_j · χ_{[1−γ, 1)}({kγ}),
where χ_A denotes the characteristic function of A. Define a two-dimensional potential V : ℤ² → ℂ by
  V(m, n) := s_1^{λ_1}(m) + s_2^{λ_2}(n).
Let H be the bounded operator on ℓ²(ℤ²) given by
  (Hψ)(m, n) := ψ(m+1, n) + ψ(m−1, n) + ψ(m, n+1) + ψ(m, n−1) + V(m, n) ψ(m, n).
A compact subset S ⊂ ℂ is called a Cantorval if S equals the closure of its interior and no connected component of S is isolated.

Question: Do there exist values λ_1, λ_2 ∈ ℂ for which the spectrum σ(H) is a Cantorval?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. Recent work (e.g., "A naturally appearing family of Cantorvals", 2024) and surveys on quasicrystal spectral theory describe the conjecture that a separable two-dimensional Fibonacci Schrödinger operator can have a Cantorval spectrum in an intermediate coupling regime: weak coupling yields an interval and strong coupling a zero-measure Cantor set, with the intermediate regime unresolved. No proof of existence of parameters producing a Cantorval has been reported.

status_evidence.title: A naturally appearing family of Cantorvals
status_evidence.snippet: Cantorvals may appear as the spectrum of a discrete two-dimensional Schrödinger operator with separable aperiodic potential given by the Fibonacci sequence in both directions in an intermediate coupling regime.
status_evidence.claim: The Cantorval spectrum conjecture for the 2D separable Fibonacci Schrödinger operator is discussed as still open, with recent results providing related families of Cantorvals.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: there exist values of λ1, λ2 such that σ(H) is a Cantorval.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open conjecture in a survey of open problems on mathematical quasicrystals.
